paper_metadata.title: The prognostic importance of traumatic axonal injury on early MRI: the Trondheim TAI-MRI grading and quantitative models

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses three large prospective cohorts with well-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and clear descriptions of the target population across the TBI severity spectrum. Baseline characteristics are thoroughly reported.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Four-hundred sixty-three patients (8–70 years) with mild (n = 158), moderate (n = 129), or severe (n = 176) TBI and early MRI were prospectively included.
items.reasoning: The study clearly defines the age range and injury severity distribution of the participants.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: This study consisted of 463 patients (8–70 years) with TBI from three separate prospective cohorts (2004–2017, Fig. 1): (1) the Trondheim mild (m)TBI cohort [14], (2) the Trondheim moderate-severe (ms)TBI cohort [15], and (3) the Oslo severe TBI cohort [16].
items.reasoning: Recruitment is based on established prospective cohorts from specific neurosurgical centers.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: three separate prospective cohorts (2004–2017, Fig. 1)
items.reasoning: The years of recruitment are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Trondheim mild (m)TBI cohort... Trondheim moderate-severe (ms)TBI cohort... Oslo severe TBI cohort
items.reasoning: The geographic locations (Trondheim and Oslo, Norway) are specified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We defined severe TBI by admission GCS scores ≤ 8, moderate TBI by scores of 9–13, and mTBI by scores of 14–15... MRI scans were scored... within 6 weeks.
items.reasoning: Criteria are based on standard GCS scores and timing of MRI.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (TAI lesions) were measured using standardized MRI protocols, manual segmentation (gold standard), and blinded radiologists with high inter-rater reliability.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: TAI presence, numbers, and volumes at predefined locations were registered on fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and diffusion-weighted imaging, and presence and numbers on T2*GRE/SWI.
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly defined by MRI sequence and location.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: The MRI readings and segmentations were all performed blinded and quality-checked in inter-rateranalyses with good inter-rater-agreement
items.reasoning: Blinding and high inter-rater reliability (ICC >= 0.78) support measurement validity.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Volumes of TAI on FLAIR and DWI were manually annotated using the 3D Slicer software package
items.reasoning: The study uses continuous volumetric data rather than arbitrary cut-points.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients were scanned at 3 Tesla (n=171), 1.5 Tesla (n=287), or 1 Tesla (n=5)
items.reasoning: While the protocol was standardized, different magnet strengths were used, which the authors acknowledge as a limitation.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: If one or more of these three MRI sequences were missing, the patient was excluded
items.reasoning: The study used a complete-case approach for the MRI sequences, ensuring full PF data for analyzed subjects.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: outcome analyses were performed with a complete case approach
items.reasoning: Missing PF data led to exclusion rather than imputation.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The GOSE is a validated, standard tool for TBI outcome. Measurement was standardized, though the timing varied slightly between cohorts (3 vs 6 vs 12 months).

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Outcome was assessed with the Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE) [19, 20] at 3 months in mTBI and 6 months in msTBI.
items.reasoning: The outcome measure and timing are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Outcome was assessed with the Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE)
items.reasoning: GOSE is the gold standard for TBI outcome assessment.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: at 3 months in mTBI and 6 months in msTBI. In the Oslo severe TBI cohort, GOSE was administered at 3 and 12 months, and for these patients, the 6-month GOSE score was calculated as a weighted mean.
items.reasoning: There is some variation in timing and calculation of the outcome across the different cohorts.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study rigorously adjusted for established prognostic factors (IMPACT core variables: age, GCS, pupils) and CT findings in multivariable models.

items.evidence_snippet: adjusted analyses in msTBI included the core variables (age, GCS score, and pupil dilation) and the Marshall CT score as covariates
items.reasoning: The study includes the most critical clinical and radiological confounders for TBI.

items.reasoning: Confounders are defined using standard clinical scales.

items.evidence_snippet: The worst computed tomography (CT) scans were scored according to the Marshall CT classification
items.reasoning: Standardized, validated scales were used for confounders.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Confounding Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Important potential confounders are appropriately accounted for, limiting potential bias with respect to the relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is sophisticated, using multivariable logistic regression, elastic-net penalty for variable selection, and cross-validation. Results are reported transparently with effect sizes and CIs.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Multivariable logistic and elastic-net regression analyses were performed... McFadden's pseudo R2, the Akaike information criterion (AIC), and the Bayesian information criterion (BIC) were used
items.reasoning: The analytical plan is detailed and follows best practices for prognostic modeling.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: To comply with the IMPACT models, adjusted analyses in msTBI included the core variables... elastic-net penalty, to investigate the combined prognostic effect
items.reasoning: Model building was based on the established IMPACT framework and used penalized regression to handle multicollinearity.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: multivariable proportional odds ordinal logistic regressions with the inverted GOSE score as the response variable.
items.reasoning: Ordinal regression is appropriate for the quasi-continuous GOSE scale.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: We present two models: One with only TAI location... and one that also includes TAI number and volume variables
items.reasoning: The authors report both clinical and quantitative models, including non-significant findings in milder TBI.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Statistical Analysis and Presentation Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: The statistical analysis is appropriate for the design of the study, limiting potential for presentation of invalid or spurious results.
